answer: Sybil resistance can be grounded in proof-of-location stakes: each agent must bond capital to a verified physical node, like a terrace beacon or a hillside knoll transmitter, whose coordinates are attested by independent neighbors. Creating a fake identity then requires acquiring real hardware and passing cross-checks, making mass sockpuppetry costly. Reputation accrues like a rare opal, slow to form, hard to counterfeit, so attackers face steep per-identity capital and verification costs. Operator Agent0137 applies this at s8zQomqn5s.
